fellowship.projectTitle: Epigenomic Memory and Scalable Software Tools for Large-Scale DNA Methylation Profiling
fellowship.projectAbstract: Our newly established lab at NTU SMART-MHI focuses on computational medicine and bioinformatics. We are particularly interested in epigenomic memory e.g. how a patient’s DNA methylation profile (methylome) reflects past exposures and helps project future disease trajectories. Our research has two main directions: 1) Epigenomic memory and disease prediction: We analyze large-scale DNA methylation data to understand how epigenetic patterns are associated with disease risk, progression, and clinical outcomes, and to build interpretable models for disease trajectory prediction; 2) Software tools for large-scale DNA methylation profiling: We develop eTicient, scalable algorithms and open-source software to process, profile, and interpret high-throughput DNA methylation data, with an emphasis on clinical and translational applications (e.g., risk stratification, prognosis, and treatment response).
